gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-esteban: Esteban is a classic serif with a lowercase that looks oversized next to its capitals, and thin strokes barely lighter than the stems. Esteban's quiet manner lets Amadeus, wide and wire-bent, earn its keep in big, short lines.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-faustina: Wide, stubborn tubing up top, then a softer cadence below. Faustina, a classic serif with fuller stems and slimmer links, gives Amadeus something gentle to lean against.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-halant: Broad, bold and cut with one nib. Halant brings a faint thick-thin shift and outward-flaring terminals, so Amadeus feels sturdier and more human beside it.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-hedvig-letters-ser: Amadeus stretches its words wide with every stroke at one width, while Hedvig Letters Serif adds heavier verticals and a sturdy body. Its strongest quality is that tension.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-marcellus-sc: Wide and wire-straight, Amadeus leads with a stroke that never varies. And Marcellus SC, a text serif with gentle modulation and pulled-back terminals, carries a long passage with a dignified, literary hush.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-montagu-slab: Montagu Slab brings robust downstrokes and slender turns beneath the heading. Amadeus stretches wide in uniform wire-like strokes, and the slab serif answers with a sensible thick-thin difference.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-hentaig: Amadeus stretches its words wide, each letter looking bent from a single wire, with gaps between curve ends and stems. Noto Serif Hentaigana, a classic serif, rewards a closer look with modest contrast and small letters nearly as tall as capitals.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-ovo: Commanding, that is Amadeus, with its single fixed nib width and wide stretch. Ovo, a serif with gentle swelling on its curves and a tall middle band, softens the page below it.
gen-dafont-amadeus-satoshi: Amadeus is wide, bold and drawn with a constant stroke. Satoshi, a sans-serif with a soaring x-height and approachable, uniform strokes, is the pair's strongest quality, a loud voice meeting a friendly one.
gen-dafont-amadeus-work-sans: Amadeus stretches wide and bold, commanding the top of the page. Work Sans, a sans with high mean lines and open c tips, suggests itself for smaller sizes, leaving the heading to go big.
